intent: Keep the race 7 geometry except for one change: body_length 0.18 to 0.12 m, which reduces yaw inertia by about 38 percent with no change to sensors, track, wheels, mass or body width. I expect slalom line loss to fall below 1 and max_error to fall below 0.06, with at least some slalom finishes appearing. I expect oval finishes to hold at 18 or more of 20 and s-bend to stay near 13 to 16 of 20. I am not committing to a wheel_track change (0.10 m) yet; it is a possible next step if this test shows yaw response is still the limit, and it would need a controller rescale. I am also keeping the mass at 0.8 kg; a lower mass would cut inertia further but also change traction, so I will not change it alongside this test.
learning: Race 7 showed slalom still loses the line at 1.2 events with max_error at the limit after gain tuning, and that sensor reach (race 3) and density (race 6) do not fix it. Next race: if slalom line loss falls below 1 with body_length 0.12, yaw inertia was the limit and the shorter body should be kept. If slalom line loss is unchanged or worse, yaw inertia is not the limiter, and the next geometry test should be wheel_track 0.10 with a controller rescale. If oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.35, the faster yaw response needs kd tuning before any further geometry change.
rationale: Race 7 (606.82 in race 5, 636.91 in race 7) confirmed the five-sensor platform: five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03, y = 0.06, with the tuned controller. Oval finishes 20/20 and s-bend 16/20, but slalom finishes 0/20 with 1.2 line-loss events per run and max_error at 0.063. The Integrator's rule says that when slalom still loses the line at 1 or more with max_error at the limit after gain tuning, the platform is limiting, so a geometry change with a clear hypothesis is needed. Earlier spread changes (race 3, ±0.04 m) and density changes (race 6, seven sensors) did not fix slalom, so sensor reach and coverage are not the cause. The off-track limit is 0.06 m for every allowed body_width, so body width gives no benefit. The hypothesis I am testing is yaw response lag. Yaw inertia is mass*(body_length^2 + body_width^2)/12. At body_length 0.18 m it is about 0.0031 kg m^2. Slalom needs fast direction reversals, and lower yaw inertia should let the turn command reach the line faster. Reducing body_length from 0.18 m to 0.12 m cuts yaw inertia by about 38 percent, and body_length has no other effect on dynamics or the off-track limit. I am making this the only change against race 7, so any change in slalom line loss can be attributed to it. The sensors stay at y = 0.06, which is now at the front edge of the shorter body, so the sensor lead is unchanged. The Integrator's optional wheel_track change (0.10 m) is deferred: it changes turn authority and needs a controller rescale, so I will not stack it on this test. I expect slalom line loss to fall below 1 with max_error below 0.06, and oval and s-bend to hold near race 7 levels. If the Integrator reports oscillation rising with the same gains, the faster yaw response is the likely cause, and the next step is the controller's kd, not a return to the old body.
